decisions.area: Medicine units, fractional stock and precision

recommendation.canonicalUnit: Smallest unit actually dispensed or measured for each medicine; define per medicine, not globally.
recommendation.countableForms: Default integer quantities for tablets, capsules, strips, vials and bottles unless that medicine is explicitly approved for fractional dispensing.
recommendation.liquidsAndMeasuredForms: Use an explicit measurable base unit such as mL; configure allowed scale per medicine.
recommendation.packageConversion: Store explicit integer conversion factors (for example pack-to-tablet) with effective date; snapshot conversion on every purchase and sale.
recommendation.rounding: No implicit rounding. Reject quantities with more fractional digits than the medicine's approved scale.
recommendation.stockStorage: Store exact scaled integer quantities; SQL precision is a storage choice, not permission to dispense fractions.

ownerMustConfirm: Canonical unit and allowed fractional quantities for each medicine category
Who may approve a medicine's unit conversion/precision change
blocks: Domain schema freeze for medicine quantity precision
Operational stock migration for affected medicines
evidence: Examples of real package contents and dispensing practice

recommendation.sellableRule: Returned medicine is never sellable by default. It can re-enter sellable batch stock only after documented inspection confirms unopened/sealed packaging, intact condition, traceable original batch, acceptable storage history and valid expiry.
recommendation.decisionMaker: A Pimpinan-designated medicine-responsible person records inspection; approval authority and eligible staff list must be configured.
recommendation.failedInspection: Keep quarantined or record rejected/expired/loss with a reason; never silently delete or re-stock.
recommendation.lineage: Return must reference original invoice line and original batch allocation.

ownerMustConfirm: Named/role-based person authorized to certify resale
Whether any opened or patient-held medicine can ever be resold
Inspection evidence required
blocks: Sellable stock restoration from patient returns

recommendation.candidate: Snapshot each package component's gross charge and discount allocation at checkout. Use exact integer-Rupiah allocation with a deterministic largest-remainder tie-break only if source audit confirms it matches the existing clinic calculation.
recommendation.returnBasis: Partial component return reverses its original snapshot allocation; never recalculate using current package prices.
recommendation.constraint: The sum of component allocations must equal the invoice/package discount exactly.

ownerMustConfirm: Approve source-matched allocation as the rule for new invoices
Conditions for refunding already-delivered service components
evidence: Representative package receipts and partial-return examples

recommendation.default: Maker-checker: requester cannot approve their own expense.
recommendation.threshold: Make approval thresholds configurable; until approved, require a separate approver for every expense.
recommendation.audit: Store requester, approver, decision time, amount, category, evidence and reversal link.

ownerMustConfirm: Approver roles and monetary thresholds
Emergency exception and evidence procedure

recommendation.classification: Separate opening float, cash advance, expense evidence, reimbursement and repayment.
recommendation.advance: An advance remains an outstanding accountable advance until receipts/settlement are submitted; do not immediately count it as an expense.
recommendation.reimbursement: Link reimbursement payment to an approved expense so it is not recorded twice.
recommendation.reporting: Petty cash is not omzet; opening float is not revenue or profit.

ownerMustConfirm: Allowed categories
Advance settlement deadlines
Who approves and who holds petty cash
blocks: Final petty-cash posting and reporting policy
evidence: Current petty-cash categories and sample records

recommendation.stock: Supplier-return request has no stock effect; approved dispatch posts one negative movement against the original batch.
recommendation.creditRecognition: Do not reduce supplier payable merely because goods were dispatched. Recognize a supplier credit only after supplier-issued credit note or other approved settlement evidence.
recommendation.paidInvoice: For a previously paid invoice, record a supplier receivable/credit balance until cash refund or offset is evidenced; do not rewrite historical payment.

ownerMustConfirm: Accepted proof for credit note/refund/offset
How long a dispatched return can remain unsettled
Who approves settlement evidence
blocks: Supplier credit recognition and payable reduction
evidence: Sample paid and unpaid supplier return cases

recommendation.targetModel: Allow multiple payment events and partial allocations through a payment-to-payable allocation ledger.
recommendation.invariants: An allocation cannot exceed the payment amount or the remaining payable balance; each payment needs date, method, source account and evidence/reference.
recommendation.legacy: A legacy lunas/paid boolean is status evidence only; never synthesize missing payment events or dates.

ownerMustConfirm: Whether partial and combined payments occur in practice
Required settlement evidence and allocation workflow

recommendation.default: The cashier who closes a shift cannot verify their own close.
recommendation.workflow: Preserve opening float, expected cash, counted cash, variance reason, verifier identity and timestamp as separate fields/events.
recommendation.authority: Verifier role allowlist and exception path must be configured; do not infer whether Admin, Pimpinan or both can verify.

recommendation.confirmedWorkflow: Cashier submits; Admin performs first-stage review; Pimpinan makes the final refund decision; payout is a separate Pimpinan-only action.
recommendation.obligation: Approval creates a refund obligation, not a cash outflow.
recommendation.payout: Record actual payout date/time, amount, method, source cash drawer/bank account, recipient/reference and evidence. Require a transfer reference for bank transfer.
recommendation.method: Prefer returning through the original payment channel where feasible; record an authorized exception and reason otherwise.

recommendation.revenue: Keep posted invoice/service revenue distinct from whether the payment has settled.
recommendation.cash: Cash receipt enters the relevant cash drawer only when actually received.
recommendation.nonCash: Transfer/QRIS/card payment starts as reported or pending_settlement; it enters bank/clearing balance only when verified by bank/provider evidence.
recommendation.fees: Record provider fees separately so gross patient payment, fee and net bank settlement reconcile.
recommendation.failedOrReversed: Preserve failed/reversed payment events; do not leave them counted as settled funds.

recommendation.valuation: Use documented supplier purchase cost or another explicitly approved valuation source; never infer HPP from selling price.
recommendation.missingLineage: Do not invent batch or supplier history. Quarantine untraceable quantities for review; keep unknown HPP visibly unknown instead of presenting false profit.
recommendation.legacyDataset: The prior migration decision register records the old Firebase operational dataset as dummy/testing data. Classify and reconfirm each source before importing it as genuine history; do not silently promote fixtures to opening balances.

recommendation.confirmed: Keep A and B as separate selectable/displayable lanes; do not merge PR13 behavior without separate review.
recommendation.candidateCallPolicy: One active call per lane (per_lane) is the preferred candidate so A and B can progress independently; implement only after confirming the operational meaning of each lane.
recommendation.events: Call, recall, cancel-call and transfer are append-only events; recall preserves the same ticket; transfer records old/new lane and retains ticket identity.
recommendation.display: Changing the TV view must not reset calls or ticket counters.

recommendation.reporting: Exclude unresolved timestamps from date-sensitive reports until reconciled; preserve original record and review trail.

decisions.area: Electronic medical record retention, correction and legal hold

recommendation.source: Permenkes 24/2022 Article 39: electronic medical records at a healthcare facility are retained at least 25 years from the patient's last visit; after that they may still be retained if useful.
recommendation.correction: Correct clinical/identity errors by an attributable amendment/correction event; do not silently overwrite historical clinical facts.
recommendation.legalHold: Suspend deletion/destruction when a dispute, investigation, audit or legal hold applies. Destruction must follow applicable legal procedures.
recommendation.privacy: Apply purpose limitation, role-based access, patient rights and documented deletion/destruction handling under applicable personal-data law.

ownerMustConfirm: Who authorizes corrections and record release/export
Legal-hold activation/release roles
Retention handling for non-clinical operational data
blocks: Automated retention/destruction jobs and clinical correction workflow until approved
evidence: Legal review of current applicable rules

decisions.area: Audit retention, export and legal hold

recommendation.auditLog: Server-authored append-only audit; operational roles cannot edit/delete authoritative events.
recommendation.retention: Use an approved retention schedule aligned to financial, employment, clinical and legal obligations; do not invent a single retention duration for all audit categories.
recommendation.export: Include date range, actor, event type, target, request/correlation ID, checksum and export audit event.
recommendation.legalHold: Pause purge for affected records while a legal hold/investigation exists.

ownerMustConfirm: Retention durations by audit category
Who can export and approve exports

blocks: Audit purge schedule and export privilege activation

recommendation.interim: Keep Firebase Authentication as the identity provider during the operational data migration; verify its bearer token on the server and map immutable provider UID to one internal user ID.
recommendation.authority: Resolve role and active state from the server-owned identity/role tables; never accept role, actor or UID asserted by browser payload.
recommendation.protectedAccounts: Keep the five protected email identities and linked records intact; verify UID/profile/role read-only before any identity migration.
recommendation.recovery: Implement email change, account recovery, disable/reactivate and UID rebind as explicit privileged workflows with approval and audit; no implicit provisioning or reactivation.
